question.text: An AMC wants to launch a new "ESG Thematic Fund" while it already operates an existing "Infrastructure Thematic Fund." Under SEBI's scheme categorization rules, is this permitted?

answer.text: Yes, because Sectoral/Thematic is one category but different themes (ESG vs Infrastructure) are treated as different sub-categories allowing multiple schemes
No, because the one-scheme-per-category rule prohibits having two thematic funds
Yes, but only if the existing Infrastructure Fund is merged into the ESG Fund
No, because ESG is not a recognized SEBI category for mutual funds

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI's categorization norms, the one-scheme-per-category rule has an exception for Sectoral/Thematic funds: AMCs may launch multiple schemes under this category as long as each scheme covers a different sector or theme. SEBI has also introduced ESG as a separate sub-category under the thematic category, so an AMC can operate an ESG Thematic Fund alongside an existing Infrastructure Thematic Fund. The Trap: Option B ignores the sector/thematic exception to the one-scheme-per-category rule. Option D is wrong because SEBI has specifically recognized ESG as a thematic sub-category. Option C's forced merger is unnecessary given the exception. Note: NISM Series V-A workbook (pages 53 and 55) supports the sector/thematic exception and the introduction of ESG as a sub-category under the thematic category.
